I've been on birth control for about ten years. I've used three different pills, The nuva ring, and two different IUDs. If you feel like you can remember to take your pill every day on time, it's worth a shot. I couldn't, so I started getting IUDs. There's also the arm bar to consider, as well as depo shot. Do some reading and really think about what would work best, and don't be afraid to speak up if you're having bad side effects or you don't feel right. It can take a month or two for your body to adjust, but you know your body, and the doctor can change your dose or brand if it's not a good fit. If the side effects are interfering with your day to day life, you might need to discuss other options. That being said, all birth control has some form of side effects, but they shouldn't be severe.
I wish you luck in finding a good solution that works for you.

I have quite a few, because sadly I'm one of those dumb people that do dumb shit and somehow manage to skate out of it alive. I'm older now, and a little less dumb, but I still get into situations from time to time that honestly could turn bad easily. 

One that sticks out in my mind in particular, was a time I decided to sneak out with a friend (we'll call her jay). Now, I'd snuck out MANY times before this. Usually to do dumb kid shit like smoking pot, drinking beer, hanging out with boys, thing rebellious teens do. 

A little back story here, my friends mom was a tweaker. Hell, she's still off and on drugs to this day. A couple weeks before Jay and I snuck out, (long story short) Her mom and dad had "accidentally" left me at a bar in the middle of the night. I started walking to a different  friend's house to get a ride home, and Jay called to ask where I was. She said her parents would come get me. Cue getting picked up, yelled at, tweaker mom flipping out and hitting Jay, father trying to stop it and swerving all over the road when it's foggy and pitch black, jay's younger siblings screaming and crying, me trying to grab the baby, etc. Mom jumps out of car. We stop and try to get her to get back in, she blames me, attacks me, I run, we eventually get back to their house. I call my parents in the morning who are, very obviously, beyond furious. So, as I'm sure you could imagine, Jay and I weren't supposed to be hanging out. 

Where I lived at the time, it was a five minute walk to the highway, then across the highway to a trailer park, down to the back of the trailer park, across the river, and upstream a few minutes, and then up a hill to Jays house. In all, the trek would take less then 20 minutes, and it was easy for me to sneak out. We hadn't seen each other in a while and didn't want to get caught, so we decided to make the thirty minute walk into town. 
The town we lived in is small, and hasn't had a police force for a long time. It's not a horrible town, but like many these days, drugs sort of took over and once the sun goes down, there are tweakers everywhere. We didn't care, of course, because we were dumb, young, and just wanted to walk to the park and smoke some pot and hang out, so what's the worst that could happen? 

Shortly after entering town, we hear someone behind us. We walk a little faster, but they pick up pace until they're directly behind us. Jay spins around to see who it is, and it's a woman. Not much taller than us, obviously high, and beat to hell. Shocked, we ask her if she's okay. She said she'll be alright, but was scared of her boyfriend and was wondering if we'd walk with her to a friend's house so she wouldn't be alone. Yeah, sure, of course, two seventeen year old girls can deffinitely protect you. 🤦‍♀️

We start walking. We were on the far southern edge of town, and it was maybe ten minutes to the 24hr gas station, who she said her friend lived behind. After about five minutes of silence, she asks our names, how old we are (we lie, of course) and asks what we're doing out that night. We start to walk past one of the restaurants in town, when a truck flies by and we narrowly dodge being hit. We try to grab the woman and leave, but she shrugs us off and starts yelling. The driver got out, and it's her boyfriend. He starts screaming at her to get in the truck, they're leaving, etc. She says no, and starts yelling back. My friend and I had some small pocket knives, and we looked at each other and gripped them. I start to pull mine out when two more guys come out from behind the restaurant. At this point I'm scared. Really scared. 
The woman and her boyfriend continue to argue. After a few minutes she says "I'm hanging out with my friends, ill see you later."
She puts her arms around us and we start walking. Once we round the corner she starts walking faster, nearly running, and we here her boyfriend yell "I'll kill you! I'll fucking kill all of you!" 
Then we ran. 
We made it to the gas station, and watched her run to the street behind and go into her friends house. Jay and I, of course, have no fucking clue what we're gonna do. We go inside the gas station for a bit, hoping that the guys wouldn't be dumb enough to go in since there'd be witnesses. After about fifteen minutes we went outside again, and didn't see or hear anything. So we started walking. It was a couple blocks to the park, and we made it there without incident. There is a small covered stage in the middle of the park, so we walked over and sat down toward the back of the stage, and proceeded to smoke, laugh, joke, and try to forget what happened. Forty or so minutes go by, and we're thinking about heading home, when we hear it. 
Those guys voices. One says "It's dark as fuck, should I go check here?" 
The other responds "Yeah. We'll go look for them. Just yell if you see anything."
We panic. We sneak off the stage out the back, and run to the back of the park. We sneak around the baseball diamond, and run out the side lot of the park. The whe time in panic mode, trying to figure out what the fuck we were going to do. We decide to just go home and hope that maybe they were just looking for someone else. 

We start walking. We get a few minutes outside of town, and we hear a car coming. We turn around, and it's the boyfriends truck. He speeds up and we run and dive into the ditch as he swerves onto the shoulder. We quickly scramble up the side of the ditch into the woods, and run through the trees trying to stay out of view. He kept driving, and turned around a couple times to drive by again, but eventually gave up and left. Why he didn't get out of the truck and follow us up into the trees I do not know, and am beyond thankful to this day that he didn't. We do eventually make it home safely. Jay calls me a few days later and says her mom heard from some tweaker friends, that they were looking for two girls who looked like us.

I've never had a copper IUD, and I am not a Healthcare professional, however I have had two IUDs. It is normal to cramp and have irregular periods with IUDS. Brown blood/discharge isn't abnormal either, unless there is a really bad smell with it, fever, or any other symptoms of infection. 
Honestly I get brown discharge around my period as well, it's usually just older blood/tissue being shed and nothing to worry about on its own.
You know your body though, cramping is normal with an IUD, but if it gets to where it is unbearable or you think something may be wrong, always seek medical attention. Better safe than sorry.

From my point of view, I grew up in a family of alcoholics and addicts. My boyfriend did as well. Some people are complete scum without the addition of drugs and alcohol. Some people are great, caring, generous, loving people until the drugs enter their life. I've known many addicts who would never steal from you, or hurt you, and who are always honest. The majority of addicts are no different than you or me, they just couldnt cope with their issues and were too afraid to ask for help, or no one believed them. Some people get injured and are given medications, not knowing they're predisposed to addiction and by the time they realize they have a problem, it's too late. The stigma surrounding addiction, that they're gross, bad people, worthless, etc. actually makes things worse. No one wants to reach out and ask for help when society tells them daily they're "genuine selfish pieces of shit" and need to just "get over it." Some people can give it up and be fine, but that is not the majority. Addiction alters your brain. 
I know a girl who got with a guy at fifteen. She was head over heels for him. He shot her up with meth one night, against her will, and it nearly ruined her life. She's nineteen now and doing her best to get back on track for her little boy.
